open_questions: Star shows strong spot variability (amplitude ~10736-19625 ppm) but dip period 0.713 d is not a multiple of rotation 2.991 d; long-term monitoring for starspot systematics remains open.
Duration is shorter than central for the TIC radius; radial-velocity mass and chromatic transit would confirm the 2.7 Re object as planet vs brown-dwarf at short 0.713 d period.
dossier.public_summary: TESS finds a steady 2.7 Earth-radius flat-bottom dip every 0.71 days on a nearby M dwarf, seen in 174 transits across six sectors with no odd/even difference, no secondary eclipse and a centroid on the target star. The size is planet-like and the signal carries no sign of a background blended binary. Variability is from starspots at a different period, leaving a small sub-Neptune as the best explanation.

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed box shape, not V-shaped, favours a transiting object over a grazing EB.
Planet-sized (well below 10 Re), not stellar/eclipsing-binary size.
Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; closest plausible neighbours are >48 sigma away.
No significant secondary eclipse at phase 0.7362 (threshold 5); EB would typically show a secondary.
No odd/even depth difference; depth_odd_ppm 4548 vs depth_even_ppm 4173 consistent within red noise, so not a binary at 1.43 d.
Depth steady across 6 sectors with 29-34 transits each and transit_depths p_consistent 0.228 from 175 transits, share_top3 0.085 - not driven by a few events.
Observed 0.4963 h shorter than central 0.842 h implies impact parameter b~0.145 consistent with the fit, not inconsistent with M-dwarf (rad 0.3648 Rsun).
Independent classifier rates it planet-like as the median known planet, with 5 similar TESS candidates all confirmed as planet.
